classification.difficultyReason: Combine the tangent–radius right angle, equal radii and the triangle angle sum.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.sourceRegion: Fourth row, middle column, part ddd
spec.description: Circle with centre O, bottom tangent contact T and horizontal tangent extending both ways to P on the right. Two radii and their joining chord form an isosceles triangle. The right circumference vertex remains unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: The chord makes 36 degrees with the rightward tangent. x is between OT and the chord at T; y is the triangle angle at the unlabelled circumference vertex; z is the central angle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 36-degree angle and unknown labels x, y and z appear in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at $T$.
$$\begin{aligned}x+36^\circ&=90^\circ\\x&=54^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The two radii are equal, so the triangle's base angles are equal.
$$y=54^\circ$$
Angles in a triangle sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned}z+54^\circ+54^\circ&=180^\circ\\z&=72^\circ\end{aligned}$$
